newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Charge laid over Australia options trades-ASC.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Charge laid over Australia options trades-ASC.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Monday it had laid a charge against one person over unusual trading in TNT call options before the successful takeover bid for the transport group by Dutch telecommunications and postal group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN).
"A charge has been laid against one person in respect of structured cash transactions that occurred immediately prior to the unusual options trading," the ASC said.
"The charge is to come before St James Local Court (Sydney) on February 3, 1997," it said.

Earlier investment bank Macquarie Bank said one of its executive directors, Simon Hannes, had been charged under the Financial Transaction Reports Act in connection with an investigation into the TNT options trades.
The bank said Hannes would plead not guilty to the charge.
The ASC did not name who had been charged and a spokeswoman was not immediately available for comment.
Macquarie advised TNT on the KPN bid.
Hannes is a senior executive of the bank's corporate advisory division, but was not part of the team working on the TNT transaction, Macquarie said.
Hannes had been on extended leave from Macquarie from August 1, 1996, but was available for part time consultation, Macquarie said.
Macquarie shares closed down 31 cents at A$8.44, after touching A$8.90 in early trade, equal to its 12-month high.
